Relevant text: 'Dropped due to a firewall rule': a test packet can be denied by a blocking VPC firewall rule or firewall policy rule; a higher-priority deny is a possible cause; the result is a configuration analysis ('the actual data plane might allow the packet through due to connection tracking'). That hierarchical firewall policies are evaluated before VPC firewall rules, the goto_next action, and the result's naming of the policy and priority are from memory of the Cloud NGFW pages (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. Since 14:50 the orders app (VMs in 10.20.0.0/16) cannot connect to its PostgreSQL VMs (10.30.0.0/24) in the same VPC. Nothing changed in the project. At 14:45 the security team attached a new hierarchical firewall policy, sec-baseline, to the 'prod' folder. The evening order peak starts at 16:00.
handover: The project's VPC rule allow-app-db (priority 1000) allows 10.20.0.0/16 to 10.30.0.0/24 on tcp:5432.
sec-baseline is owned by the security team; their on-call is reachable.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the folder's hierarchical policy, the VPC's own rules and the app-to-database path they both evaluate.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

effects.finding: The intent is a guardrail against outside access, not a block on the app.

goto.label: With the security on-call: add rule 900 to sec-baseline, goto_next for 10.20.0.0/16 to 10.30.0.0/24 on tcp:5432

neteng@cloudshell:~$ gcloud compute firewall-policies rules create 900 --firewall-policy sec-baseline --organization 1234 --direction INGRESS --action goto_next --src-ip-ranges 10.20.0.0/16 --dest-ip-ranges 10.30.0.0/24 --layer4-configs tcp:5432 --description 'orders app to db: defer to VPC rules (SEC-1290)'

writeup.question: For the record: what dropped the traffic, how you fixed it without losing the baseline, and how the next policy change is checked.

parts.label: What
parts.modelAnswer: The Connectivity Test reported 'Dropped due to a firewall rule': sec-baseline on folder prod, priority 1000, deny tcp:5432 from 0.0.0.0/0. Hierarchical policies are evaluated before VPC rules, so allow-app-db was never reached.

parts.label: Fix
parts.criteria: A narrow exception with the owner.
parts.modelAnswer: With the security on-call, rule 900 goto_next for 10.20.0.0/16 to 10.30.0.0/24:5432 hands this path to the VPC rules. Detaching the policy would have removed the guardrail from every project; raising the VPC rule's priority changes nothing.

parts.label: Next change
parts.modelAnswer: Security now runs saved Connectivity Tests for app paths before attaching folder policies, and the tests re-run nightly.

baselineDetached.headline: An exception, not a removal
baselineDetached.body: The policy was right for outside access and wrong for one internal path. A goto_next rule for that path, agreed with the policy's owner, keeps the guardrail.

peakFailed.headline: Hierarchical rules come first
peakFailed.body: A deny in a folder or organization policy ends evaluation before VPC rules. Find it with a Connectivity Test and fix it in that policy.

scoring.modelReasoning: A Connectivity Test names the drop: the new folder policy denies tcp:5432 from everywhere, and hierarchical policies are evaluated before the VPC's allow rule. With the policy's owner, add a narrow goto_next rule for the app-to-database path so the VPC rules decide it, and leave the baseline in place. Detaching the policy removes the guardrail; VPC rule priority cannot outrank a hierarchical deny. Test before future attachments.
